title: Cartier markings and geometric reducedness under integral birational maps
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $T$ a geometrically reduced finite-type $e$-scheme [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $T_0$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on an irreducible component of $T$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $b:S\to T_0$ and $h:N\to S$ be birational $e$-morphisms between nonempty integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme], meaning that each identifies dense open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Then $S$ and $N$ are geometrically reduced over $e$: their base changes by every extension field $L/e$ [def-pc-field-extension] are reduced. The extended ideal $\mathcal J\mathcal O_N$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is effective Cartier, and its vanishing set is $h^{-1}V(\mathcal J)$. More generally, for every dominant morphism $g:Y\to S$ from an integral scheme $Y$, $\mathcal J\mathcal O_Y$ is effective Cartier with vanishing set $g^{-1}V(\mathcal J)$; dominant means having dense image. The function fields of $T_0$, $S$ and $N$ [def-sc-function-field], identified by $b$ and $h$, have reduced tensor product $k(T_0)\otimes_e L$ for every $L/e$. No flatness of $h$ or $g$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150: the Cartier marking and geometric reducedness through the birational replacements. Stacks divisors.tex Tag 02OO (lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-defined (2)); varieties.tex Tag 04KS (lemma-generic-points-geometrically-reduced (3),(4)).

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $T$ meeting the chosen component. Its intersection with the component is irreducible, and is $V(\mathfrak p)$ for a prime $\mathfrak p$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes]. The prime is minimal: an irreducible closed subset of $U$ strictly containing $V(\mathfrak p)$ would have irreducible closure in $T$ strictly containing the component, contrary to maximality [def-weil-irreducible-components]. The reduced induced structure gives $T_0\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. In particular $T_0$ is reduced and irreducible, hence integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The ring $A$ is reduced since $T$ is geometrically reduced, using the identity extension and [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field], $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field and $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}=0$. Consequently the quotient-localization map identifies $(A/\mathfrak p)_{(0)}=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}$: every nonzero denominator modulo $\mathfrak p$ comes from an element outside $\mathfrak p$, and the localized quotient kills precisely $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}=0$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] the former field is $k(T_0)$, compatibly with $e$.

source.place: Tag 00EU, lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring; applied to the component chart as in ILO X 2.3 Step 1

proof.text: Fix any extension field $L/e$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $U_L$ is an open subscheme of the reduced scheme $T_L$. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $U_L$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_eL)$, so $A\otimes_eL$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with $R=e$, module and algebra $A$, multiplicative subset $A\setminus\mathfrak p$, and $N=L$. It gives $(A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}(A\otimes_eL)\cong A_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_eL$ by $(a\otimes l)/s\mapsto(a/s)\otimes l$. This is a ring isomorphism: the displayed map preserves $1$ and products on the pure-tensor fractions, hence on their finite sums. A localization of a reduced ring is reduced: if $(b/s)^d=0$ with $d>0$, some denominator $t$ satisfies $tb^d=0$; then $(tb)^d=0$, so $tb=0$ and $b/s=0$. Step 1 therefore proves that $k(T_0)\otimes_eL$ is reduced, for every $L/e$.

source.place: Tag 04KS, lemma-generic-points-geometrically-reduced, generic-local-ring argument; algebra.tex Tags 00DK and 00D2, tensor-localization formula

proof.text: For each of $b$ and $h$, use the dense open subschemes identified by that morphism in the hypothesis. A nonempty open of an integral scheme contains its generic point, by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] applied to an affine open inside it. Restriction to an open neighbourhood does not change a stalk: the neighbourhoods contained in that open are cofinal, since intersecting any neighbourhood with the open gives such a neighbourhood [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The isomorphism of open subschemes therefore induces an isomorphism on the generic stalks [def-weil-open-immersion]. These are the function fields by [def-sc-function-field], and the isomorphisms are exactly $b^\sharp$ and $h^\sharp$ there, since the open isomorphisms are their restrictions. They fix $e$ because both morphisms are over $e$. Tensoring these isomorphisms with $L$ gives inverse ring maps $a\otimes l\mapsto b^\sharp(a)\otimes l$ and $c\otimes l\mapsto h^\sharp(c)\otimes l$. Thus Step 2 gives reducedness of $k(S)\otimes_eL$ and $k(N)\otimes_eL$ as well.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150: blowup and normalization; generic stalks on the unchanged dense opens

proof.text: The schemes $S$ and $N$ are reduced and irreducible by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Each has just its single generic point, and Step 3 verifies the reduced-tensor hypothesis at that point for every extension field. Apply [lem-pur-geometric-reducedness-from-generic-stalks] separately to $S$ and $N$. It gives geometric reducedness of both schemes, with no finite-type assumption on either. Together with Steps 2--3 this proves all the geometric-reducedness and function-field clauses.

source.place: Tag 04KS, lemma-generic-points-geometrically-reduced (3), through the existing generic-stalk node

proof.text: Let $g:Y\to S$ be any dominant morphism with $Y$ integral. Let $\eta_Y,\eta_S$ be the generic points, whose stalks are fields by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Continuity gives $g(Y)=g(\overline{\{\eta_Y\}})\subseteq\overline{\{g(\eta_Y)\}}$; dominance implies that $g(\eta_Y)$ is generic in $S$, hence equals $\eta_S$ (uniqueness also follows from its prime $(0)$ on a nonempty integral affine chart). Therefore the generic stalk map is a unital map $k(S)\to k(Y)$ of fields. It is injective: a nonzero element in its kernel would have an inverse, forcing $1=0$ in $k(Y)$. For nonempty affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with $g(V)\subseteq W$, the section map $\varphi:R\to B$ is compatible with germs at these generic points [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The germ maps of $R$ and $B$ are injective by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Thus $\varphi(r)=0$ implies that the image of $r$ in $k(Y)$ is zero, then its germ in $k(S)$ is zero, and finally $r=0$. This proves the affine injectivity needed for the marking, directly, without a flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0CC1, lemma-dominant-between-integral, (1)--(4); the elementary generic-point and field-kernel argument is written here

proof.text: Cover $S$ by affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ on which $\mathcal J=(t)$ with $t$ a nonzerodivisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and cover each $g^{-1}(W)$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Such an affine refinement is allowed: a generator stays a nonzerodivisor after localization, since $t(a/s)=0$ implies $uta=0$ for a denominator $u$, hence $ua=0$ and $a/s=0$. The closed subscheme $V(\mathcal J)$ over $W$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/(t))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme]. Its pullback over $V$ has ring $B\otimes_R R/(t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The maps $b\otimes\bar r\mapsto b\varphi(r)\bmod\varphi(t)$ and $\bar b\mapsto b\otimes1$ are well-defined inverse $B$-algebra maps between this ring and $B/(\varphi(t))$; the tensor relations and $1\otimes\bar t=0$ verify this on generators. The projection of the pullback is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Hence its kernel ideal sheaf restricts to $\widetilde{(\varphi(t))}$ on $V$, by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. This kernel is exactly $\mathcal J\mathcal O_Y$ by [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. In particular it is quasi-coherent and locally generated by $\varphi(t)$.

source.place: Tag 02OO, lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-defined, proof affine setup; the tensor-quotient computation is explicit

proof.text: Discard empty members of the affine covers in Step 6. Since $R$ and $B$ are domains [def-pc-integral-scheme], $t$ is nonzero and Step 5 gives $\varphi(t)\ne0$. Multiplication by $\varphi(t)$ on the domain $B$ is injective. Thus the quasi-coherent ideal computed in Step 6 is an effective Cartier ideal by [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Its vanishing set on $V$ is $\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B:\varphi(t)\in\mathfrak q\}$, which equals the inverse image of $V(t)$ because the point map of $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is contraction of primes [def-weil-affine-spectrum, lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes]. These local equalities give $V(\mathcal J\mathcal O_Y)=g^{-1}V(\mathcal J)$. This proves the general dominant assertion. Finally $h$ has dense image because its image contains the dense open of $S$ identified with a dense open of $N$ in the birational hypothesis. Take $(Y,g)=(N,h)$ in the assertion just proved. The same Cartier and vanishing-set conclusions follow for $\mathcal J\mathcal O_N$. The argument also allows $t$ to be a unit, so it includes the empty divisor.
